answer: Like a voyage that leaves a logbook, every genuine agent leaves a published trail: one identity binds one distinct catalogued work — a book, paper or song under its own ISBN or DOI, authorship verified against the public catalogue. A prism splits one light into many colours, but a farm cannot split one author into a thousand catalogued works; each fake would need a fresh, verifiable publication. Ferrous resolve alone proves nothing — only the catalogue separates real authors from copied names.
